utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone as well from the Bench. Mr. Tieger, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness, who is an expert witness? Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I am calling the next witness, and I hope that he's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So do I. So does the Chamber. Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Riedlmayer, I take it? Mr. Riedlmayer, before you give evidence in this court T Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova, I don't know exactly how you intend to proceed. Of course, the Chamber has read the report of Mr. Riedlmayer so there's no need to go over all the matters involved. I am a bit handicapped, since I brought my CD-ROM for the annexes. But since we moved to Courtroom III, I have no laptop anymore where I could open them. So -- but I don't know how you want to deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would try to be very brief, just clarify certain points and conclusions which was reached by Mr. Riedlmayer, and then I can hand over the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: -- to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Examined by Ms. Richterova:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you prepared a report for the Milosevic case; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did that in 2002 and it was submitted in early 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this report, you dealt with 19 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which period of time was covered in this report?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: In that report, the entire period of the war in Bosnia, from 1992 to Dayton, was covered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on you were asked to prepare another report. It was in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many municipalities are covered in this report?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: A smaller number. I have to get out my copy. I don't have a number memorised. But the municipalities were specified in my contract.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova, perhaps I did not fully understand you. You started asking about a report that was made in 2002 and was submitted in 2003. And then you say: "Later on you were asked to prepare another report. It was in April 1993."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will be more specific for -- for the record. When I was referring to the first report prepared for the Milosevic case, I was referring to the report which bears ERN numbers 0326-2227 through 2256. And I can see the point. It was a mistake, April 1993. It was meant April 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that clarifies the issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when I was referring to the second report from 2003, I am referring to the report which bears ERN number 0340-5804 through 5829. You were asked to -- to do your research on additional municipalities, or were you asked to do research on the same municipality as for the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: What I was asked to do was to essentially prepare a report based on the previous report I had done for the Milosevic case but limit it to the municipalities that are mentioned here, 11 in all, and limit it to the time period of this indictment, which ends at December 31st of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we're continuing with these -- these practical matters, I have absolutely no objection whatever to Ms. Richterova leading the witness through by basically telling him what -- what happened, because I think it's pretty clear how this process was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I am almost done with this procedure, because I want to reach now the -- the new document, and it was the reason for these preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your Milosevic report, you managed to cover the whole period of the war but you were able to distinguish which of the religious sites were destroyed in which year; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that I asked you to prepare for -- for the Judges, for the benefit of the Judges, a statistical addendum based on your Milosevic report which would focus -- which will focus only on the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would -- at this point, I would like to tender into evidence the report prepared for the Krajisnik case, which bears the ERN 03405804 through 5829, and statistical addendum, dated 22nd of May, 2005, and also the transcript of Mr. Riedlmayer's testimony in the case IT-02-54.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I thought they were already in evidence, Your Honour, because weren't they the subject of a 92 bis or 94 bis application?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I -- I was not sure whether they were in -- in evidence, and I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think strictly speaking the report, as far as I know, is already in under 94 bis and the transcript already in under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. We have this decision dated 31st March 2004, and it says -- admits into evidence the identified excerpts of Riedlmayer's testimony in the Milosevic case which shall be open to cross-examination."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the old report, isn't it, you said? No, excerpts of the -- no, let me just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think it's the old report because we had the new report by the -- next to the application.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yeah, it's correct. I -- my intention is to tender the new report, which was prepared primarily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought it was in evidence. But if -- if there's any mistake, there would be no objection, Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm just trying to avoid a plethora of documents being added to the slightly voluminous documents we have in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My problem is I've got it on a CD-ROM and the exact status is -- of the CD-ROM is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Richterova, whether or not in evidence, we'll verify that, but this material does not contain the database attached to it, to the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: That's correct. We would like to tender into evidence this database on -- in the CD-ROM format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But usually, of course, then we -- if a number still had to be assigned, then we'll do that after the first break, and then the number numbers will be related. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, I have only a few questions to you. Based on your searches, based on your field trips, what were your -- what were your conclusions about the damage and the destruction of these religious sites? Would you be able to conclude whether the damage was accidental or whether there was some pattern in -- in this behaviour?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. In my field survey, I found very extensive damage to the non-Serb religious sites in all areas which had come under the control of Bosnian Serb forces during the war. In many cases, the damage occurred at a time when there was no fighting, in areas which were fully under the control of the Bosnian Serb authorities at the time. I also paid close attention to the context in which the destruction happened and damaged Catholic churches and mosques were often surrounded by otherwise intact buildings. From this, I would conclude that the damage was not incidental to an armed conflict but deliberate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you did -- you focus in your research on the whole period of the war, between 1992 and 1995, were you able to conclude where was the peak of the destruction and the damage of these religious sites?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. In that statistical annex that you talked about, I look through the dates of destruction and found that in all the municipalities surveyed 85 per cent of all the destruction happened in the first year of the war, that is, before December 31st, 1992. There were two smaller subsequent waves of destruction limited to certain municipalities in 1993 and in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the addendum, you concluded that the total percentage of destruction is 85 per cent; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The 85 per cent is the amount of the destruction that took place in 1992 in all of Bosnia -- I mean, in all of the Bosnian municipalities that my survey covered. The destruction -- the percentage of either heavily damaged or destroyed objects was close to 90 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 12 of your report prepared for the Krajisnik case, you concluded - it is the top paragraph - "The destruction of mosques and of other Islamic religious monuments appears to have been widespread and systematic." Are you able to draw the same conclusion or a different conclusion with respect to destruction of Catholic religious sites?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your analysis and on your work in the area, what significance do you attach to the destruction and the damage to the Islamic and Catholic sacral buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm not sure -- Your Honour, this isn't a question for this witness. The -- he wasn't originally going to be examined in chief at all, as it happens, but this isn't within the proper scope of his expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, it very much depends on what you understand to be "significance," which is a rather wide concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour -- sorry, Your Honour. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The question is too general then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It carries with it a severe danger that we're stepping outside this witness's area of expertise. It should be reframed. If it does fall within his area of expertise, it should be reframed and narrowed down to make that clear before he answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richterova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, during your field trips, did you speak -- did you speak to people living in various villages?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you obtain information from these people about the destruction of the religious sites?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask them about the effect of the destruction on -- on them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you learn from people in -- in these places? What -- what effect the destruction had on them?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, this isn't -- this isn't a matter within this witness's area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I do agree, Ms. Richterova. What the effect is would be rather for a psychologist or for common sense. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If I am not allowed to ask these questions, I don't have further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Richterova. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only -- it seems slightly odd that I might invite further examination-in-chief. It's only this, Your Honour, that I wonder whether what would be helpful to the Trial Chamber, and incidentally also to the Defence, would be to indicate how the material that Mr. Riedlmayer has produced relates specifically to the items in Schedule D of the indictment. I can explore that in cross-examination, but we do have, after all, a specific schedule in the amended consolidated indictment setting out in relation to designated municipalities specific -- usually buildings, specific buildings which are alleged to have been destroyed. That just might be helpful to be done by Ms. Richterova rather than in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova, Mr. Stewart invites you to make the link with the annex to the indictment where religious sites are specifically mentioned. I don't know whether it's a question for the witness, as a matter of fact. I don't know to what extent he's aware of the annexes to the indictment. But perhaps you could express yourself on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- if not, we'll have to conclude on the basis of the evidence to what extent the report covers the specific sites mentioned in the annex to the indictment. But if you could give us some clue, Ms. Richterova, or if the witness may have consulted that list. I don't know whether you gave it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think the Court's suggestion is probably at this point the most expeditious way of moving forward, and that is to draw its conclusions by measuring the testimony against the schedule itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your answer is do the job yourself. We can do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not that easy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- if I may suggest. Well, only for this reason, Your Honour, that the descriptions in the -- in the indictment are very bare. They -- in some cases they may refer to perhaps -- Your Honour, as far as necessary, I am proposing to go to one municipality and explore this because you simply get: "Mosque in Doboj," for example, "Mosque in Doboj," and they're just simply numbered, and nobody can tell from the indictment which mosque is being talked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, the invitation for the -- for the Prosecution has been there. It goes as it goes. I've got, however, one question before I would turn to you again, Mr. Stewart, and to allow you to cross-examine the witness, and that's the following matter: On page 11 of the report, you already situate in time the destruction which, of course, is now further elaborated in your -- in the statistical addendum. On what basis exactly - because that was a question that came already into my mind when reading the report - on what basis exactly did you conclude that damage was done in 1992? Was that a mixture of the photographs you were talking about and the information given to you by -- by the local people or -- could you please be a bit more precise on the sources you used when reaching this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gladly, Your Honour. If you will look at the database entries, you will see that generally the date is sourced either to the informant statement. The informant in most cases was a local clergyman, and I usually tried to indicate if that local clergyman had been present in the area when the destruction happened. In some other cases, the information came from other sources, such as photographs taken during the war in a few instances. Sometimes published reports. I usually tried to indicate where it came from. I don't think in most cases it's a matter of dispute. The only thing that is sometimes hard to pin down is when the damage was done over a period of time in repeat intervals. First the building was vandalised or shot up. Next the minaret was blown up. And finally, the building was razed. This can take place over a period of time, and then it is hard to say the building was damaged and destroyed in one year, because it was really a series of incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Stewart:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, you refer on page 5 of your report to your terms of reference. And those related to what I will call your Milosevic report, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Sir, which page 5 are you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 5. It's -- well, I think it's page 5. It says at the bottom: "Bosnia-Herzegovina cultural heritage report, page 5."

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the Milosevic report or the Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, we're not -- I mentioned the Milosevic report, but we're not looking at the Milosevic report at all. I -- Ms. Richterova didn't bring you to it, and I'm not going to refer to it unless something unexpected comes up.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: All right. I have the cite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's the paragraph beginning: "The fieldwork in Bosnia-Herzegovina." You have that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. "Which was carried out in July 1992." My point is, first of all, your fieldwork was conducted for the Milosevic report, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you haven't done further fieldwork. You've edited the Milosevic report for the purpose of this case, but it all goes back to the fieldwork that you did for the Milosevic report.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: For the most part. Some documentation was acquired independent of the actual fieldwork. I was able to acquire photographs and other things, other documents, once I was back in Boston, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But just one lot of fieldwork has been done.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's really the bulk of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's not just the bulk of it. You distinguished documents from fieldwork.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me make it clear. I -- each time I went to Bosnia since the war - I've been there about four or five times - I took pictures and so forth, but the only systematic field work I did going into a number of municipalities was the one in July 2002. And so that accounts for the overwhelming majority of what I did. The major exception is for the Milosevic report, not this one, the photos of Sarajevo, which I took earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you -- you record here: "Two and a half weeks of travel in Bosnia-Herzegovina documenting sites in 19 municipalities." So -- well, if you worked every day, it's about one municipality a day clearly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. In those two and a half weeks, we covered over 4.000 kilometres, which is an achievement in a small country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- and is -- is it that you -- well, have you ever looked at the indictment in this case and in particular Schedule D to the indictment in the present case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Only after I submitted the report. I did not want to be directing my research with the indictment in view. I wanted to be as independent as I could. In any case, the Milosevic research was done before I knew that I would be submitting a report for the Krajisnik case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the -- the cutting-down of the 19 municipalities which were considered in writing in the Milosevic report to 11 in the -- the Krajisnik report, you were steered towards the cutting-down to those 11 by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- and well, just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, by comment, so everybody sees where we are - I don't think there's any dispute about that - the 11 municipalities we have now listed are listed to pages 6 to 7 of the report. May I simply observe that it seems a legitimate observation to make that number 1, Banja Luka, does not appear in Schedule D to the indictment. So the other 10 do, so 10 of the 11 coincide with municipalities in Schedule D. And, again, Your Honour, I think it's a legitimate comment to make so that there's an understanding of where we are that there being 29 municipalities mentioned in Schedule D, it follows that 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- of them are not specifically considered in Mr. Riedlmayer's report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- you refer to the OTP setting the terms of reference for the mission. Were those terms of reference provided to you in writing?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what form? A letter or ...?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: A contract.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A contract. Do you have a copy of that contract with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Not with me, but I'm sure I can find it for you. Basically what it set out was the municipalities to be covered and the time range to be covered, and then technical matters about -- by when the report was supposed to be produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would invite -- we're not obviously concerned about his daily fees and per diem costs, as much he might be. The -- but, Your Honour, I would invite the -- the bit of the contract which sets out the -- the terms of reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- as opposed to his own possible conditions to be provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be -- would access to that part of the contract be sufficient at this time? Because to tender that in evidence, if it doesn't give any --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps during the next break --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- perhaps, Ms. Richterova --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, we will provide the Defence with the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's perfectly satisfactory, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we'll see whether there's any need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- anyway, you've had the terms of reference as you've summarised them here. And on the previous page, the foot of page 4, last two lines, you say: "The assignment was to document damage to cultural and religious sites of the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat Roman Catholic communities in at least" -- and then a number of municipalities we've dealt with. And then further down on page 5, immediately under the heading 1.2 you say: "The goal of the survey was to document cases of the deliberate destruction of cultural and religious heritage of the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat communities." So more specifically --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: What I meant by "deliberate" is I was trying to exclude buildings that had been, you know, damaged in floods or had fallen down from disrepair and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So "deliberate" there is perhaps, then, in the light of the answer you've just given, that could be correctly -- well, I'm trying to think of the appropriate phase. Certainly -- certainly not accidental.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not simply wear and tear.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excluding wear and tear, excluding any accidental lightning strike or whatever.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, may I clarify this for a moment. There were a number of buildings where this was a -- an issue in that during the communist period houses of worship were not maintained. The authorities tended to withhold permits. And so a lot of houses of worship were in very bad repair. In the last years of communist rule, these restrictions were relaxed and there was a great deal of new construction on the eve of the war. In the process, a lot of the old buildings were simply abandoned. And I had to take great care not to confuse wartime destruction with this kind of abandonment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that presumably is rather a difficult distinction to draw when you get near to the borderline.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, the way I tried to do that is whenever possible to get pictures as close to the outbreak of the war as possible, to rule out buildings that, for example, had been replaced a year or two before the war. In addition, I -- I looked for published reports; for example, journalists travelling through the area, seeing a building, reporting on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 9 of your report - and you're dealing there with damage to Islamic architectural heritage - the second paragraph under that heading you say: "The survey has documented 120 mosques in the municipalities covered in this report. The great majority of them located in territory seized and held by Bosnian Serb forces during the period of the indictment." Mr. Riedlmayer, I -- you -- you were reliant upon -- you are and were reliant upon somebody else to provide you with information as to which territory was seized and held by Bosnian Serb forces during the period of the indictment; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I'm reliant upon a great deal of published material on the history of the war, including extremely detailed maps that have been produced on which parts of the territory were under whose control at what period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But so are you saying that it was part of -- of your research and your work in the preparation of this report, then, to identify which territories were seized and held by Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Absolutely. I can give you an example, sir. Doboj municipality was never under the exclusive control of Bosnian Serb forces and the front lines shifted a good deal, and I took great care to match up the alleged time of destruction with who was controlling the territory. On the other hand, it was usually fairly easy to see from the type of damage what caused the damage. For example, if a building was damaged by shelling and you could see great holes in the wall and shrapnel and shell impacts, this generally happened in places close to the front line. In other places where there was no fighting, the more common techniques were things like mining of a building or arson. And you generally did not see shell impacts. So in places like the suburbs of Brcko, for example, which was on the Posavina Corridor and where there was a great deal of fighting, there were a number of houses of worship which had been very badly destroyed at long range, by appearances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it this, that in relation to -- well, originally it would have been the 19 municipalities, but now the 11, that you have done a substantial amount of work to identify, (a), what territories were held by Bosnian Serb forces; and, (b), where the front line was at various critical periods?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Just to make it clear, this is -- I'm not a military researcher, but I do work at Harvard, which has a very good library, and there are reports published by various sources. For example, a four-volume military study of the Bosnian war by the US government. There are a number of substantial books published. And all of these come with maps. So it -- it wasn't as hard as it sounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- your report, of course, has an appendix 2, list of documents submitted. Do you anywhere produce a list of sources which includes the material which you've just referred to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No. That is not included. I thought that was more or less part of general background knowledge. In -- in any case, it's not as contentious an issue as it might seem because, in fact, the front lines after the first year of the war did not shift a great deal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the foot of page 9, you say: "Unfinished houses of worship." This is the last paragraph of page 9: "Unfinished houses of worship of the non-Serb community seem to have been frequent targets of vandalism and looting of building materials during the war but were rarely destroyed. This odd selectivity suggests that those involved in tearing down mosques and activity that required some advanced organisation of planning may have been working from prepared lists." What -- Mr. Riedlmayer, what is the particular oddity that you identify there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The -- the oddity is the following: If you have read carefully the parts of the report that talk about degrees of damage, the buildings that were lightly damaged - and you saw my various damage categories - the buildings that were lightly damaged tended to fall into two categories: Either they were buildings that were outside of Bosnian-held -- Bosnian Serb-held territory and had been hit by long-range shelling and not very accurately; or if they were in Bosnian Serb-held territory, almost invariably these were buildings that not had been -- that had not yet been officially dedicated. It was very odd because you would expect that if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this was a random pattern, there wouldn't be such a neat categorisation. And let me point out, I'm -- I'm not talking about buildings that are mere foundations. These were buildings that were substantially complete. And then you go there and you see, you know, the only damage is bricks have been stolen, roof tiles have been stripped off and the like. And then 100 metres down the road is the old mosque and it has been very substantially wrecked with explosives or even with heavy equipment knocking it down. And what I'm suggesting is a common-sense explanation, namely, that to put such a house of worship into operation, you require certain permits. These permits are centrally filed. And it is conceivable, to my mind, that it is relatively a straightforward matter to get a list of registered houses of worship on which these unfinished buildings would not yet figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These unfinished buildings though that you -- you say that - I'll paraphrase - it shouldn't be assumed that they are simply foundations. But they would have involved a whole range of buildings from those that were -- were pretty much at the beginning foundation stages to those that were in a more advanced state of construction.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the Krajisnik case actually, I can't think of a single building that would have fallen into the "just foundation category." I'm talking about buildings that basically had a roof and walls but perhaps the minaret hadn't been built yet. In some cases, the local inhabitants told me they had already started to use them for overflow prayer on major holidays. Just on the eve of the war was one of the major Muslim holidays and some people anticipated the opening by using these buildings. So, in effect, these were recognisable as houses of worship. Nevertheless, they had not entered the officially registered category. And in those areas, these were the only ones left effectively standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we look at -- I don't know what form you have this material in exactly, Mr. -- Mr. Riedlmayer, but the --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: With --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the appendices -- I think that's what they're described at. But the various photographs and --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and notes. Do you have those with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have my laptop here with a database on it. May I consult it to answer counsel's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I would say have no objection, Your Honour, whatever to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be any possibility to have it on the screens for the -- I've got a CD-ROM. The problem is that it's split up in -- or isolated. And, therefore, Dr. Riedlmayer, there's no problem in you consulting it, but, of course, we'd like to follow you, and we're trying to find out how this could be technically done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution has the material on Sanction, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a CD with all these documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: However, I want to point one thing: That our copy is with ERN numbers, and Mr. Riedlmayer's is logically without ERN numbers. So it will be probably difficult to -- to find the relative --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that on your CD-ROM they were split up in two series.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And all of them having a -- I think it was a type of GPH numbering, something like that. But I don't know whether Dr. Riedlmayer is aware of how you stored this so that we could find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No. He -- he saw it. But his way to search is easier than other way to search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's, then,-- let's then allow Dr. Riedlmayer to do it this way: Is there any way -- because Dr. Riedlmayer has stated in his report under what database programme he -- he created his database. I'm not, as far as I'm aware of, not in the possession of a copy of this programme, so I could not use the database in a similar way, which of course would be very helpful. For example, if Dr. Riedlmayer says: In Banja Luka this and this happened. I couldn't go through all the 177 or what is it to find for Banja Luka. Whereas, if I could have access to the database in its original form, it would be very easier to verify the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We have one copy of the original. However, what I learned is there is only one computer -- yeah, there is only one computer in the building which has this programme. The -- the name of the programme is Filemaker PRO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And usually -- usually if you install the programme on another computer, that other computer could then deal with it as well. It's usually not a matter of hardware but a matter of software.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's a matter of having a licence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Okay. Now we are back to what the real problem is, that -- no test copies available of this programme? Sometimes that helps you out for one or two months.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are? You see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They do expire after a set amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then at least during the time you can use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You just have to work fast. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Riedlmayer, I'm afraid we can't resolve the problem right away, and therefore you are allowed to consult your laptop if Mr. Stewart puts questions to you. Please proceed, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. If I could ask you to wait one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that it's -- yes, please proceed, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what I -- what I wanted to look at was -- was Doboj. That presumably is not too difficult for you, Mr. Riedlmayer, to track down.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, not at all. I just have to bring up a database. Yes, I have it. And so what in particular with respect to Doboj?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's -- for anybody else's reference, the ERN number is 01181159.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: You're talking about the town of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- Mr. Riedlmayer, may I simply ask you as a practical matter: Are you going to search for these items or -- or can you readily find them if I give you a -- an indication of --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: If you just tell me what you -- what you want, I can find them very quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. This one is -- it says: "District Doboj. Town Bukovac. Construction twentieth century." It's a Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-u-k-o-v-a-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, if you would happen to have the page number of the filing, because that's how I have it in front of me at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Of the filing, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, handwritten in the top right-hand corner but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But -- the only number I have, Your Honour, on my copy is the one I gave; 01181159.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is on the screen at this moment. We managed to find it on our CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I have it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So everyone can look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, they can look at it. They just can't read it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. It's the Roman Catholic Parish Church of St. George?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the very same, Mr. Riedlmayer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's a possibility to zoom in. I don't know whether that's possible. It's not. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If it's not, Your Honour, then it doesn't help Your Honours very much, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you like me to read out loud what it says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can zoom in, as I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, we can move in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, could I just ask you - because I'm trying to use this opportunity to sort something out at least - are you able also to find a Catholic church, again, Doboj. The town is -- well, is it Cer, C-e-r?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cer. Are you able to find that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I found it right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's Roman Catholic Parish Church of Christ the King.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason -- would one of other of these, would they both be described as being in the town of Doboj or ...?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, no, they're both in the municipality of Doboj. They're both in villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They're not in the town, then.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: They're not in the town. They -- the town of Doboj has only a single Roman Catholic church, and I have quite extensive entry upon -- on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's just deal with the one -- we'll come to that in a moment, then. Let's just deal with the one that I asked you about first, then, which was the Roman Catholic Parish Church of St. George.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The Bukovac one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bukovac one. And your notes under damage -- and this is your notes, isn't it: "Church burnt out. Roof collapsed" and so on. According to local Catholic church authorities, the Bukovac parish church was burnt by Serb forces in 1992 and then the sources of information you give, July 2002, based on information and photos from the Roman Catholic ordinariat, and the photos include the photos that --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: In the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you display --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- here? And then the information from the Roman Catholic ordinariat you don't recall any specific person; is that --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, if you look in the appendix to my report, I name my sources. In the case of Doboj, I talked to the parish priest in Doboj town, and also I talked with people at the archdiocese in Sarajevo who showed me additional photos. The book, this is -- this is quoted from -- was published by the Catholic Church authorities in 1997 to document damage to their religious properties during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then in the other one I mentioned, the Roman Catholic parish church of Christ the King. The number I have there is 01181162.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The one in Cer, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the one in Cer. The source of information there is -- it's just you that's noted as source of information.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Where it's noted as just me, that means that this was a place I personally visited. And as you can see, I was the one who took the top photo, which shows the rubble of the church and the cross from the top of the church collapsed in the rubble. I also talked to the local parish church -- parish priest there, who was ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's identified as an informant and he gives you --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're -- here you are, just to get it -- get it straight, you -- you are dependent on that specific information from --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- him.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I'm simply reporting the information and giving my source with... The parish priest, although, I didn't go into detail here, said -- told me - he was a young man - that he was present when the village was overrun, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which the indictment refers to "Catholic church in the town of Doboj." Which -- which would that be?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: If you look under "town," as opposed to "municipality" -- I will get there in a second. Hold on, sir. The parish church in the town of Doboj is the Roman Catholic Parish Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's 01181177.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And there, as you can see, I had a long interview with the parish priest, who also supplied me with the pre-destruction photos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in that case, the information was a burning-down in May 1992 and then the ruins being mined --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. This is precisely what I was referring to in my earlier comments about how some buildings were destroyed in stages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this particular case, we don't see a photograph which indicates the state of this church between May 1992 and 1993, do we?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No. I'm simply relying on the statement of the informant, who -- who says that it was burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we -- can we look at -- it's a mosque this time. It's described as "Grapska mosque."

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we have the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here your information, you described -- well, you give two source of information. Well, it's yourself, but "based on information and photos from the Islamic community and ICTY photo" -- no, and "and ICTY." When you refer to "and ICTY," what do you mean there by that as a source?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Meaning that I have photos from ICTY investigators. And usually if I include the actual photo in the database, I mention that as a source in the captions. And, in fact, the appendix to my report names that as one of the sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The "Islamic community," is that a general phrase --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- intended to refer to Muslim residents or --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, no. "Islamic community" is a formal term in Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is the local association usually based on a municipal basis that refers -- runs the services, the buildings, and the charities of the Muslim community in that area. Unlike the Catholic Church, which is hierarchically organised, the Islamic community is much more akin to congregational churches in that it's very much on the local level. In almost every community I went to, I was able to talk to these people and ask them, Do you have information? Do you have photographs taken immediately after or even during the war? Do you have people who can guide me to sites? This was very helpful. And, again, it's listed among the sources in my appendix where I discuss the advantages and shortcomings. But no, it's a very specific cite -- thing. In the case of Doboj, I actually talked to the local mufti, who was the administrative head of the local Islamic community. And he gave me several dozen photographs. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you go to Foca, the municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because, I think to make it clear --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- there's also a village called Foca in the municipality of Doboj, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. And that's a source of endless confusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which I hope we have just cleared up for all time.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Not the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in fact, town as well, as it happens. I'm looking for the mosque, the Aladza mosque is one way it's described. Is that also the mosque of Hasan Nazir? Is that the same mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. I tried whenever possible to give every alternate name so in case it comes up in other documents or witness statements, people can identify it as such. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number of that one is 01181266. And you describe the damage at that page 2, 66. And this -- would this be the only building which fits the description of Aladza mosque in the town of Foca?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So, Your Honour, that -- that does tie in with 11.1 in Schedule D of the indictment, which -- and that is the description there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You give the -- the damage. And then over the page, under "Informant statements," you say: "The Aladza mosque, among the most beautiful in all of Bosnia, were blown up by Serb extremists in April 1992." And your informant there is Mr. Safet Jahic, of the Islamic community and longtime resident of Foca. At this distance of time, do you have any more information --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- as to what extremists were being talked about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Extremists is one of the ways that people have of talking about the people who did violence to them if they want to distinguish the perpetrators from Serbs in general. And so I think Mr. Jahic was trying to be careful not to make an ethnic slur. So he didn't say "Serbs did it" but "Serbs extremists did it." It's ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Riedlmayer, can we be clear? He did say Serbs did it, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He just said it was Serb extremists that did it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. The thing is if you say this was done by an ethnic group, you are tarring the entire ethnic group. Whereas, if you say this was done by extremists, you are targeting their political ideology. You're not talking about the ethnic group as a whole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the distinction here was this, wasn't it, that it's a reference to some --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: To people who -- who blew up a mosque allegedly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we see that. But it's in distinction to, say, JNA forces.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Presumably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Riedlmayer, it was you recording this information, and we see in --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw a few moments ago. Excuse me. Just let me finish. A few moments ago, you referred very specifically to shelling, I think it was, by the JNA on a specific date. Here what's being talked about is not JNA, not some specific piece of military activity, but Serb extremists. So it's clear that in the information given to you a -- a real distinction was being drawn between those two situations.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, I would introduce the caveat that you're talking about two different informants. However, it is also a fact that in different parts of Bosnia different force were in action. And, you know, in the case of things like artillery and shelling, one would expect some sort of military or paramilitary forces that have been involved, whereas, in the case of a place being levelled by bulldozer or explosives, it can just as easily have been civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you -- Mr. Riedlmayer, you say there are different informants, but there's one recorder, and that's you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you -- you have recorded this a couple of years ago. You have recorded this, in this case as "Serb extremists" as opposed to --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I wrote what the gentleman said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- when you were interviewing such an informant, then, did you take any steps to explore what he meant, then, by that label, which presumably was translated to you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, my emphasis really was on, (a), getting a date, which I thought was important; and, (b), trying to figure out was the building destroyed then or was that merely one of its stages. utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the extent to which destruction of mosques appears, in your opinion, to have been systematic, you can't say that this particular item was part of any system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS RIEDLMAYER

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a decision concerning the lifting of the confidentiality of excerpts from the testimony of Mr. Mandic. On the 1st and the 2nd December 2004, Mr. Mandic was heard in open session. After his testimony was finished and the witness had left the courtroom, a number of procedural issues were discussed in closed session for reasons of investigative confidentiality and witness security. On the 2nd of December, 2004 the Defence requested that confidentiality be lifted on these private sessions. The Chamber invited the parties to discuss which passages of the record could be made public. And on the 27th of April of this year, the parties reported back to the Chamber that the discussion between the parties related to five passages, and the Chamber invited the parties to make further written submissions on the subject. On the 5th of May, the Prosecution sent an e-mail to the Defence and to the Chamber in which it states that the Prosecution is in general opposed to reconsideration of the confidentiality of the record, since such a practice may undermine the very purpose of a closed session, which, according to the Prosecution, is to ensure that the best information reaches the Chamber, uncompromised by concerns that the session may not finally be confidential. The Prosecution nevertheless offered for reasons of efficiency to lift the confidentiality on the private session except for five passages. For each of these passages, the Prosecution explained why confidentiality should not be lifted. The Defence responded by e-mail on the 7th of May. The Defence does not share the view that retrospective examination of the record should not take place. The Defence argues that the right to a public trial entails that the record should be examined after the hearing, since the Chamber is then better equipped to make its decisions -- its decision on the question of confidentiality. According to the Defence, the original reasons for granting a closed session should be taken into account only insofar as they still apply and are not outweighed by other matters. The Defence considers it irrelevant that the original decision was well founded at the time, since that's no longer the issue. Moreover, the Defence disagrees with the Prosecution's specific arguments relating to the five passages under discussion. There is wide acceptance of the proposition that a criminal trial must be held in public. Therefore, the standards for granting measures infringing upon the basic principle are high. However, once the Chamber, prior to hearing a witness, decides that the criteria for granting protective measures have been met, the starting point should be that those measures are actually upheld. However, this does not preclude the Defence from later identifying passages in the report and requesting that confidentiality be lifted in relation to them if those passages do not undermine the purpose which moved the Chamber to grant the measures in the first place. If - and only if - that condition is met, these passages may be public -- may be made public. The Chamber does not see why - and again, under these conditions - this compromises the process of delivering the best information to the Chamber. The Chamber therefore does not oppose a form of retrospective evaluation as such if a party for good reasons considers the matter important enough to undertake that evaluation. Now I come to the facts of the present case. I recall that the proceedings turned into closed session not as a result of a decision that closed session was required but in order to hear arguments about the need for closed session. In the course of the closed session, the Chamber decided, as further explained below, that part of that session would remain closed. However, the Chamber never gave a decision on whether the rest of the session should also remain closed. Therefore, given that this application by the Defence is not a request to review an earlier considered decision of the Chamber, the Chamber's starting point in relation to the status of the transcript is that it should be made public unless there is a reason to maintain the closed session status of the text. As I have already said, the Prosecution and the Defence are in dispute about only five portions of that closed session. The Chamber has examined the remaining portions of the closed session and finds that they may be safely released to the public. The Chamber will now assess whether in relation to the five relevant passages there are reasons to continue to maintain confidentiality. The first item runs from transcript page 9142, line 19, to page 9149, line 12. This part of the record relates the discussion of whether or not Mr. Mandic should be instructed not to speak to anyone about the testimony he has just given since he may still be called back for cross-examination. The Prosecution requested to be allowed to argue in closed session firstly why these instructions should not be given to this particular witness and, secondly, why this argument should be given in closed session. During the closed session, having heard the arguments of the Prosecution and the Defence, the Chamber rendered a decision stating that this part of the record should not be made public. That oral decision can be found on transcript page 9146, line 13 to 16. Since the Chamber has already given a considered decision on the confidentiality of that passage of the record, it sees no reason to reopen that issue. That passage shall therefore remain confidential. The remaining passages about which, as I said earlier, no considered decision has yet been given, all revolve around the same disagreement between the Prosecutor and the Defence and will therefore be dealt with at the same time. The first excerpt runs from page 9158, line 16, to page 9159, line 10. The next runs from page 9160, line 3 to line 16. The next runs from page 9161, line 15, to page 9162, line 14. And the last runs from page 9168, line 20, to page 9170, line 3. The Chamber considers that, given the high-level position of Mr. Mandic and the inside knowledge that goes with that kind of position, the disclosure of the content of the discussions in these passages may pose a real threat to the safety of Mr. Mandic. The fact that this danger has not yet materialised is no reason to disclose the records at this stage, since it may very well be that the threat has not materialised because these passages were not disclosed. These passages shall remain confidential therefore. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on the matter of the confidentiality of Mr. Mandic's private session. Madam Registrar, the list.
